thesis: An eminence-discounted Dragon deck whose engine is the ARRIVAL, not the attack: Miirym copies each nontoken Dragon that arrives, and Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas price every arrival in damage — a cascade the passing stacks resolve from an assembled board, while the turn that puts two discounted Dragons down to build it is the model's claim, not a verified line. V6 bought a response suite four of whose six additions are castable at instant speed as printed, and two of those four are flash Dragons whose own entry is an arrival; Whirlwing Stormbrood's flash grant and Sneak Attack's unrestricted activation are the main doors for any other Dragon off your own turn — Chaos Warp on your own permanent and Transcendent Dragon's free cast of a countered Dragon spell (CR 608.2g) are narrower ones — and none of it is verified.

stages.label: THE FIVE-COLOUR TOLL, PAID TWICE
stages.what_it_does:
A nine-mana commander and a curve of six-drops in five colours, and the deck pays that toll twice: 32 land entries / 35 copies, then 23 ramp copies against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' 10-12, which deck-audit calls OVER. A build choice — eminence discounts GENERIC mana — but mana-base still reads UNDER at 35 against 36-38, and colour-sources UNDER by nine on black: 21 sources with rocks and dorks against a yardstick of 30, on-curve 0.729 where every other colour is 0.822 or better.

'Ramp or fixing drawn' assembles in 0.906 of 10,000 runs at mean turn 2.268; mean available mana is 5.944 at turn five. Land drops fray, 0.756 at turn four and 0.624 at turn five, and that figure cannot be about taplands: the goldfish assumes LANDS ENTER UNTAPPED, ALWAYS, so it measures whether a land is in hand, not how it enters. On tapped lands deck-audit's taplands axis reads 1 against a ceiling of 8, verdict AT — Path of Ancestry — and mana_analysis's 12 is a superset. The other eleven are CONDITIONAL, and only six are a choice: the six shocks pay 2 life. Dragonskull Summit wants a Swamp or Mountain, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade and Smoldering Marsh two basics, and Turbulent Springs enters untapped only if OPPONENTS control eight or more lands.

Five sources are RESTRICTED per deck-facts — Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Unclaimed Territory pay for spells only. Desolation sits here, not output: its four Dragon-only mana is why it is in the 99, and deck-audit prices it as the one single point of failure, a one-card component at 0.167 assembled.

Pips explain the fetches and V6's Forest-to-Mountain: 31 cards want {R} for 48 pips, against 17 and 19 green.

evidence.note: all 15 FETCH TARGETS are lands of mine; the cartographer's own note concedes Dragonskull Summit has no basic type, so the name is true of 14
all 5 of MANA ON LEGS are my five mana dorks, and nothing else is
22 of the 23 in THE FIXING are mine; the 23rd, Dragon's Hoard, I filed under fuel for its gold counters, and Desolation of Smaug sits in hood-1 beside two red-white lands on its ritual half

Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim are three of the six in THE SETUP's LIBRARY RUN beside Enlightened Tutor, Sarkhan's Triumph and Chaos Warp, because they say 'search your library'; in this deck they are lands
8 cards carry it against 5 ramp:rock and 2 ramp:land. Three of the eight (Gadrak, Ganax, Goldspan Dragon) are Treasure Dragons I filed under fuel, so five are in this stage — exactly city-6

stages.label: THE PRICE CUT, LIVE FROM TURN ONE
stages.what_it_does:
The first thing that has to happen is a Dragon costing less than it says. Eminence is the only part of this engine an opponent cannot answer: The Ur-Dragon discounts other Dragon spells {1} FROM THE COMMAND ZONE, live on turn one with nothing on the battlefield to remove. Stack 007 step 8 rules it, citing 601.2f, and prices Lathliss at {3}{R}{R} rather than her printed {4}{R}{R} — 'a cost reduction is not optional and the printed {4}{R}{R} is not payable as written'. The four cards here stack on top of it: Dragonlord's Servant ({1} less) and Dragonspeaker Shaman ({2} less) are Dragon-specific; Urza's Incubator ({2}) and Herald's Horn ({1}) name a creature type as they enter.

What this stage buys is not one cheap Dragon, it is TWO IN ONE TURN, which is the assumption every trigger downstream is priced against — a six-drop at {3}{R}{R} plus a four-drop at three is eight mana instead of ten.

Measured: 'Cost reducer drawn' assembles in 0.523 of 10,000 runs, 0.423 by turn six, mean turn 3.253 — 0.666 and 0.55 with tutors counted. 'Reducer + ramp assembled (the turn-5-Ur-Dragon hand)' is 0.467 / 0.339. So roughly half the deck's games are played at eminence's {1} alone.

Note what this stage does NOT buy. The commander itself is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.329 of runs, mean cast turn 6.919, median 7, and is never cast by turn ten in 2,238 of 10,000. Eminence is doing this deck's ignition from a zone the game will not let anyone touch; the body is a bonus. That is also why no card here is a single point of failure — the one piece that must be live cannot be removed, and the other four are redundant with each other.

evidence.note: step 8 rules that Lathliss's total cost is locked in before any of it is paid, minus all cost reductions (601.2f), and that with eminence active from the command zone the cost paid is {3}{R}{R} — five mana, not six

The Ur-Dragon, Dragonlord's Servant and Dragonspeaker Shaman sit in THE AIR FORCE — the commander in hood-1 with the legendary Dragons, the two reducers in hood-0 THE ENABLERS beside Glorybringer, Twinflame Tyrant and Whirlwing

Herald's Horn and Urza's Incubator sit in THE GEAR with Panharmonicon, Lightning Greaves and Mithril Coat. One job, two addresses, split on card type: a creature that discounts and an artifact that discounts
exactly these five carry it, and the fifth is the commander, whose discount works from the command zone where no role tag can see the difference

stages.label: TREASURE, TWO DRAGONSTORMS THAT COME BACK, AND THE DRAW THE GOLDFISH DOES NOT MODEL
stages.what_it_does:
Once a Dragon has landed the deck needs two things it is short of: mana for the SECOND Dragon the same turn, and cards.

Six Treasure sources cover the first — Atsushi, Gadrak, Ganax, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone and Smaug the Magnificent. 'A Treasure source drawn' assembles in 0.672 of runs, 0.562 by turn six. Read the hoard as a FLOOR and not a measurement: goldfish meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names Atsushi, Gadrak and Ganax as sources it cannot see, so 0.428 Treasures at turn six and 1.853 at turn ten are what the other three produce. Treasure is a stockpile rather than a rock — it buys one expensive turn and does not raise mean available mana, which is why it sits here and not in mana.

Cards are the thinner half. deck-audit reads card-advantage UNDER at 4 copies against a floor of 10, and its own note says the count misses Dragon's Hoard and Sunbaked Canyon, which do the job in words the taxonomy has no pattern for. What actually refills: Garruk's Uprising and Temur Ascendancy each draw when a creature with power 4 or greater enters — the same event the output stage is built on, so the engine pays for its own next card — Dragon's Hoard banks a gold counter per Dragon entering and cashes them one at a time, and both Dragonstorms RETURN TO HAND when a Dragon enters — Roiling draws two and discards one, Breaching is impulse access, not a draw.

Two tutors sit here because their job is to find the missing piece rather than to ramp: Enlightened Tutor (Panharmonicon, Sneak Attack, Dragon Tempest) and Sarkhan's Triumph (any Dragon), both at instant speed. The goldfish models a cast tutor as filling one missing any_of group, which is the gap between every unassisted rate in this model and its assisted twin.

evidence.note: all six Treasure sources sit in THE HOARDING LEGENDS, a neighbourhood of THE AIR FORCE — the map groups them as the declaration does, and the scatter table marks that component coherent; the other five members of the hood are not Treasure cards

Garruk's Uprising, Temur Ascendancy and both Dragonstorms sit in hood-1 WHEN DRAGONS LAND, and they do three different jobs. Enumerated: Roiling Dragonstorm draws two and discards one; Garruk's Uprising and Temur Ascendancy each draw on a power-4 creature entering; Breaching Dragonstorm exiles until a nonland card and casts it free at mana value 8 or less or puts it in hand, which is impulse access. deck-audit's card-advantage axis counts four copies — Atsushi, Garruk's Uprising, Roiling Dragonstorm, Temur Ascendancy — and Breaching is not among them. The two Dragonstorms are here for coming back; the two power-4 draws are the draw the map cannot hear. Enlightened Tutor and Sarkhan's Triumph are in hood-0 THE LIBRARY RUN
Dragon's Hoard files in THE FIXING's ANY COLOUR hood, on its mana ability, and not with the six Treasure sources it does the same job as
exactly six cards carry it, matching the declared Treasure component card for card

stages.label: ONE ARRIVAL BECOMES SEVERAL, AND EVERY POINT BECOMES TWO
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper, in two tiers that multiply different things.

MORE ARRIVALS. Miirym copies every other nontoken Dragon that enters; Lathliss makes a 5/5 for each (oracle text — it fires on no passing board); Ancient Gold Dragon rolls a d20 on combat damage and makes that many 1/1 flying Faerie Dragons; Panharmonicon fires a permanent's triggered ability an additional time when an ARTIFACT OR CREATURE entering caused it — not an enchantment or a land. Sneak Attack puts a CREATURE CARD from hand onto the battlefield for {R} with haste — the scope stack 005 turns on — and Hellkite Courser's entry puts the commander from the command zone with haste until the next end step. That the commander tax is untouched is stack 008's answer, and 008 has not passed. Token-versus-nontoken is the brake 001 and 002 both had to settle: token copies do not re-trigger Miirym or Lathliss, so the cascade terminates.

MORE DAMAGE PER POINT. Twinflame Tyrant doubles all damage a source you control deals to an opponent or their permanents, Solphim doubles NONCOMBAT damage only, Thrakkus doubles each Dragon's power when it attacks, and Atarka grants an attacking Dragon double strike. Read against the output stage, Twinflame and Solphim both apply to Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest damage aimed at an opponent — and NONE of the four is verified: no fully-contained combo record, no passing stack.

single_point_of_failure is null by judgement. Stack 007 is brutal about ONE board — cutting Panharmonicon takes 002 from 64 damage in twelve instances to 20 in four, 'its LETHALITY, not just its margin', a 68.75% loss — but deck-audit names only Desolation of Smaug, Panharmonicon sits in no goldfish component, and the cascade runs without it.

evidence.note: Panharmonicon doubles Miirym's trigger into two nonlegendary 6/6 hasty Lathliss copies; every later entry is a token and both nontoken clauses exclude tokens, so the cascade stops
the same cast with Panharmonicon removed and nothing else changed: Miirym triggers once, one copy enters, 20 damage in four instances. The measured value of one card on one board
15 Faerie Dragon tokens enter as a single event and Miirym copies none of them — a token is not a nontoken Dragon
Sneak Attack puts Drakuseth in with haste for {R}; the same stack REFUTES it reaching the command zone (903.6 — the command zone is not the hand) and names Hellkite Courser as the card that does

8 of my 10 sit in THE AIR FORCE, spread across all four of its neighbourhoods: Miirym, Atarka and Thrakkus in hood-1, Lathliss and Solphim in hood-2 THE FIREBREATHERS, Ancient Gold Dragon and Hellkite Courser in hood-3 THE TRIGGERS, Twinflame Tyrant in hood-0 THE ENABLERS. The four damage multipliers have three addresses inside one city

Panharmonicon — the card stack 007 measures as worth 44 of 002's 64 damage — files in THE GEAR with the cost-reducing artifacts and the equipment, nowhere near Terror of the Peaks, whose triggers it doubles
Sneak Attack sits in hood-1 WHEN DRAGONS LAND, an enchantment among enchantments, while Drakuseth, the card stack 005 resolves it with, is in THE AIR FORCE

stages.label: WHAT AN ARRIVAL IS WORTH
stages.what_it_does:
What the deck points at a table, and it is priced per ARRIVAL rather than per attack. Terror of the Peaks deals the entering creature's power to any target; Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas deal X where X counts your Dragons and X is recomputed at each trigger's resolution.

Stack 002 measures one Lathliss cast into a four-permanent board at 64 damage in twelve separately-targeted instances — 36 from Terror across six triggers, 28 from Tempest at X = 4,4,5,5,5,5 under optimal ordering — which kills a 32-life seat. Stack 007 step 9 then settles the harder question: every one of those twelve instances reads 'any target', a player is a legal choice for all of them, and aimed at one seat the running total reaches 42 by the eighth instance, so that board CAN kill a player at 40. Stack 001 is the same machine larger: fifteen tokens enter as one event, every Tempest trigger sees X = 17, and 255 damage is available.

Firespitter Whelp is the odd member of the payoff tier and the only one of its four that needs no body to enter: 1 to each opponent whenever you cast a noncreature OR Dragon spell.

The rest is interaction, which deck-audit reads as 11 copies against a floor of 8 but only FOUR classes answered against a floor of five, with graveyard detected as unanswered. Enumerated: Swords to Plowshares and Generous Gift are unconditional single-target answers, Chaos Warp reaches any permanent at instant speed, Crux of Fate is the UNCONDITIONAL sweeper and one of two on deck-audit's sweepers axis, Glorybringer exerts for 4 to a non-Dragon creature, and Steel Hellkite — new in V6 — destroys every nonland permanent of a chosen mana value controlled by a player it dealt combat damage to, once each turn.

evidence.note: 64 damage across twelve instances, 36 Terror + 28 Tempest, killing the 32-life seat
X is recomputed per trigger and each of the fifteen sees 17 Dragons; Dragon Tempest is an Enchantment and does not count itself
step 9 answers (c): stack 002's twelve 'any target' instances reach 42 aimed at a single seat, so a 40-life player is killable off that board

five of my ten — Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas, Firespitter Whelp, Glorybringer, Steel Hellkite — sit in THE AIR FORCE, Terror in hood-3 THE TRIGGERS and Scourge of Valkas in hood-2 with Lathliss

Dragon Tempest, load-bearing in three passing stacks, files in hood-1 WHEN DRAGONS LAND, separated from Terror of the Peaks, its partner on the boards of 002 and 007; Chaos Warp is in hood-0 THE LIBRARY RUN on its reveal wording

Crux of Fate, Swords to Plowshares and Generous Gift sit in THE INSURANCE's hood-0 WHITE SHIELDS AND SWORDS beside Teferi's Protection — the map files answers with shields, which is fair for the instants and not for Crux, a sorcery

seven cards in the 99 carry it and four of them are here — Dragon Tempest, Firespitter Whelp, Glorybringer, Scourge of Valkas. The taxonomy sees an entry payoff whose damage happens to be aimable at a creature and calls it removal; the other three sit in mana, protection and wincon

stages.label: THE ANSWER TO 'I NOW HAVE ZERO RESPONSES'
stages.what_it_does:
Prescription 0241fb6a70f1, after five games at 1W 4L: 'speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close.' Five of V6's six spell additions land here (the sixth, Steel Hellkite, is in output), and FOUR of the six are castable at instant speed as printed — Stubborn Denial is an instant; Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood have flash; Asceticism and Steel Hellkite do not. What V6 bought is not more protection, it is protection that can be held up.

Asceticism is the only always-on PROTECTION in the 99 covering more than one creature (Greaves and Coat cover one each): board hexproof, plus regeneration for {1}{G}. Mithril Coat has flash, is itself indestructible and attaches free to a legendary creature as it enters — with 12 legendary creatures here, a three-mana flash artifact that blanks a removal spell. Stubborn Denial is {U} and hard-counters any noncreature spell while you control a 4-power creature — nearly every Dragon here. Transcendent Dragon counters a spell, exiles it and lets you cast it free: a response that is also a body every conversion trigger fires on. Whirlwing Stormbrood protects nothing itself: while it is on the battlefield sorceries and Dragon spells have flash, so mana held for a response can still deploy. UNVERIFIED — no passing stack touches it.

The five older pieces cost held mana all game, and two read 'if you control a commander' — the commander is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.329 of runs, so Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat usually are not free. interaction_castable_by_turn reads 0.306 / 0.395 / 0.481 on turns four to six, and the model's own note calls that a FLOOR. Thunderbreak Regent only PRICES removal, 3 damage to its caster; of the twelve it stops nothing.

evidence.note: 6 of my 12 sit in THE INSURANCE — Boros Charm, Deflecting Swat, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Stubborn Denial, Teferi's Protection — beside three removal cards from output. Its gloss reads 'held up, not cast', yet the three held-up FLASH permanents of V6 are elsewhere
Mithril Coat and Lightning Greaves file in THE GEAR as equipment, beside cost reducers and Panharmonicon
Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood and Thunderbreak Regent file in THE AIR FORCE as Dragon bodies
Asceticism files in hood-1 WHEN DRAGONS LAND, an enchantment among enchantments. Twelve cards, four cities

nine cards in the 99 carry it and seven are here — Asceticism, Boros Charm, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Lightning Greaves, Mithril Coat, Teferi's Protection (both protection:granted holders and both buff:attached holders are among them). The other five: Deflecting Swat carries protection:redirect, Stubborn Denial and Transcendent Dragon carry counterspell, and Whirlwing Stormbrood (buff:counters, threat:body) and Thunderbreak Regent (threat:body) carry no protection role at all — the taxonomy cannot see either job

stages.label: PROVEN ON A BOARD, THIN AS A ROUTE
stages.what_it_does:
Two cards, and the thinness is the finding rather than a hole in the model: this deck does not close with a finisher, it closes with the cascade, and every card that does that work is already earning its slot in conversion or output. What is left is the two whose only job is to end the game. Drakuseth, Maw of Flames deals 4 + 3 + 3 to any targets whenever it ATTACKS — an attack trigger, not a cast trigger, so it fires the turn Sneak Attack cheats it in and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice (stack 005). Scourge of the Throne untaps all attacking creatures and adds a combat phase the first time it attacks the player with the most life, which is the one card here that doubles an already-lethal board rather than building one.

What is checker-passed: stack 001's board kills BOTH opponents; stack 002's kills the 32-life seat with 64 damage and, per 007 step 9, can reach 42 at a single seat and so kill a player at 40; stack 005 lands 17 for {R} off Sneak Attack, four lands and a Drakuseth in hand. What is NOT checker-passed is any line that gets from an ordinary turn six to one of those boards — every stack starts from a board already assembled.

Against the goldfish's one 40-life opponent that never blocks, median kill turn is 7, mean 7.376, with 0.238 by turn six, 0.542 by turn seven and 0.052 of runs never killing by turn ten; mean board power is 14.706 at turn six and 19.642 at turn seven. Read that as an unopposed clock on ONE seat, not a win rate — and read it against the prescription that named being killed first as the problem, because a deck this fast in a goldfish is a deck a table sees coming.

evidence.note: Drakuseth's trigger is an attack trigger; 4+3+3 fires the turn it arrives and it connects for 7, and all 17 stands through the end-step sacrifice
the deck's only checker-passed board that eliminates two opponents at once

both sit in THE AIR FORCE — Drakuseth in hood-1, Scourge of the Throne in hood-3 — with every other Dragon; nothing in the map distinguishes a finisher from a body, which is the map being right, since in this deck they are mostly the same card

absent_stages.why: No fodder STAGE, re-verified against the current 97 entries, and defended on what the conversions EAT rather than on how often they run. A regex scan for 'sacrific' returns eleven cards: four fetchlands (Arid Mesa, Bloodstained Mire, Scalding Tarn, Wooded Foothills), Gemstone Mine and Sunbaked Canyon sacrifice THEMSELVES as their own cost; Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon sacrifices itself to tutor; Gadrak, Ganax and Goldspan Dragon only print the Treasure token's reminder; Sneak Attack sacrifices each creature it puts in at the next end step. None is a sacrifice outlet. A scan for 'dies|died' returns exactly two cards that turn a death into a resource: Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge ('a Treasure token for each nontoken creature that died this turn', at your end step, so only while Gadrak itself survives), the only card that pays for ANOTHER creature's death; and Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, which pays for its OWN death only (three Treasures, or two impulse-drawn cards). The choosable kills: Sneak Attack, with NO activation limit, so every {R} is another creature sacrificed at an end step; Desolation of Smaug (3 to each non-Dragon) and Crux of Fate's non-Dragon mode, which kill the five dorks, Dragonlord's Servant and Dragonspeaker Shaman and leave Gadrak and Atsushi, both Dragons, alive; Crux's Dragon mode, which kills Atsushi for its payout but kills Gadrak too; and Generous Gift aimed at your own creature. The any-target damage triggers (Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest, Scourge of Valkas, Drakuseth, Smaug) can also be turned on your own creature, at the cost of the damage they exist to deal. So there are real fodder-to-fuel conversions: Gadrak with any of those, and Atsushi through Sneak Attack, Crux's Dragon mode, Generous Gift or a 4-damage trigger, with or without Gadrak. The verdict stands on two grounds. First, the payoff side is two cards and neither is a resource the deck makes: Gadrak is one payoff, and Atsushi converts itself once, since nothing in the 99 returns it from the graveyard or to hand. Second, what is eaten is the deck's own cards: Desolation and Crux eat the deck's ramp, Generous Gift and the damage triggers spend removal or output on it, and Sneak Attack eats creature cards from hand, the deck's own Dragons, whose sacrifice is the price Sneak Attack already charges, so the Treasure is a rebate on that price, not an engine. A fodder stage would name one payoff, one self-cashing Dragon and a cost as an engine the deck is not built around. That reading is a judgement; open_questions' last entry asks the rules half.

lines.note: Fifteen Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event, so Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times and every trigger sees X = 17 (2 pre-existing Dragons + 15 tokens); 255 damage is available at a single target and the 30-life seat dies to the second. The tokens ARE what Tempest counts and what it triggers on, so the arrow is a feed and not a coincidence. This is the deck's one fully-contained Commander Spellbook line (bracket 3, 'Near-infinite damage', infinite: false), and the record stays a CANDIDATE: 001 fixes the d20 at 15 'for determinism' and starts post-combat-damage, so it verifies the line's resolution on a roll of 15 once Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected — not the connection, which needs an unblocked attack, and not the roll, which averages 10.5.

Panharmonicon doubles Miirym, so one Lathliss cast becomes two nonlegendary 6/6 copies, and those entries pay Terror 36 across six instances of 6 — of which 24 is attributable to Miirym's two copies, the other 12 being the wave-1 triggers on Lathliss's own entry, which Miirym did not cause. One-directional: Miirym makes the bodies whose entry Terror prices.

Panharmonicon doubles every trigger in the cascade, because each is caused by a creature entering — Tempest's six instances read 4,4,5,5,5,5 for 28. It multiplies the payoff and not only the bodies, and stack 007 measures the counterfactual on the same board: without it the whole cascade deals 20.

THE UN-DOUBLED FLOOR. Stack 007 step 5 rules that ORIGINAL Lathliss requires a NONTOKEN Dragon, so she makes no 5/5 on this board; the one body is Token A, created by Miirym's single trigger (step 4). Of 007's 20, Terror of the Peaks takes 12 (6+6) and Dragon Tempest 8 (4+4). Split by the entry that caused each trigger, Lathliss's own entry and Token A's are 10 apiece, and of each 10 Terror takes 6 and Dragon Tempest 4 — Terror is in neither via. Dragon Tempest damage that Miirym's body accounts for is FIVE: the 4 of Token A's own Tempest trigger (step 6), plus 1 on the wave-1 Tempest trigger, which counts 4 Dragons instead of 3 only because Token A is on the battlefield when it resolves (step 3's ordering; step 7: 'had the wave-1 Tempest trigger resolved before Miirym's, X would have been 3 and the total 19'). So this pair carries 5 of the 20. The arrow is the Panharmonicon-free version of lines[1] on the identical board, and 007 rules the 20 does not kill the 32-life seat that 002's 64 does.

The deck's only checker-passed arrow that reaches a finisher. {R} puts Drakuseth in with haste, the attack trigger fires the same turn for 4+3+3, it connects for 7, and all 17 stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice. The same stack refutes this arrow ever pointing at the commander: 903.6, the command zone is not the hand.

A CLAIM, and the null is load-bearing. Stack 007 step 8 rules the rules half — eminence is active from the command zone and Lathliss's locked-in cost is {3}{R}{R} — but 007's own scenario declares the full {4}{R}{R} paid 'so the cascade, not the discount, is what is being measured', and the scenario names no Ur-Dragon on any board. So the discount is verified as a rule and unverified as this deck's route into the cascade. What it would buy: a turn where Lathliss and a four-drop Dragon both land, which is what every trigger count downstream assumes.

The one arrow that runs from the engine back into its own fuel, and it is unverified. Ganax reads 'Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, create a Treasure token' with no nontoken clause, so Miirym's token copies should each pay a Treasure — which would make the cascade fund its own next cast. 001 and 002 both had to settle the token-versus-nontoken question for Miirym and Lathliss, and neither board contained Ganax.

V6's thesis as a single arrow, and nothing verifies it. Whirlwing reads 'You may cast sorcery spells and Dragon spells as though they had flash', so with it on the battlefield Lathliss can be cast on an opponent's end step with mana held up through the turn cycle for Stubborn Denial and Mithril Coat. It is not the only door off your own turn: Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing are themselves flash Dragons whose entry is an arrival, and Sneak Attack's '{R}: You may put a creature card from your hand onto the battlefield' carries no 'activate only as a sorcery' clause (CR 117.1b: an activated ability may be activated any time its controller has priority). If any of it holds, the deck stops choosing between developing and responding — the choice prescription 0241fb6a70f1 says it kept losing.

map_disagreements.component: THE CASCADE ITSELF — stack 002's five cards at three addresses
map_disagreements.why: Stack 002 is the deck's measured engine: Lathliss cast into Miirym, Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest and Panharmonicon, 64 damage. The map puts Miirym, Lathliss and Terror in THE AIR FORCE (and in three different neighbourhoods of it), Dragon Tempest in THE SETUP's WHEN DRAGONS LAND, and Panharmonicon in THE GEAR. The cartographer's note says as much. The reason is the space: CardBERT reads typed fields, so a creature, an enchantment and an artifact with the same 'enters' trigger land apart. The engine is a relation between card types, and the map is a grouping by card type, so the one thing the deck does is the one thing the constellation cannot draw.

map_disagreements.component: THE AIR FORCE read as an engine part
map_disagreements.why: 27 cards, 28% of the 97 entries, holding members of SIX of my seven stages: conversion 8, fuel 6, output 5, ignition 3, protection 3, wincon 2. It is not a stage, and its gloss — 'every arrival here discounts the next under eminence' — is false of FOUR members: Dragonlord's Servant (Goblin Shaman), Dragonspeaker Shaman (Human Barbarian Shaman) and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus (Phyrexian Horror) are not Dragons, and eminence discounts only 'OTHER Dragon spells', so it never discounts The Ur-Dragon, the city's fourth exception. (Read the other way — the arriving card doing the discounting — the gloss is true of only the commander and the two reducers.) What the city collects is creatures; that a deck of Dragons is mostly creatures makes it look like a reading.

map_disagreements.component: V6'S RESPONSE SUITE — six additions, four addresses
map_disagreements.why: The six V6 spell additions answer one prescription and the map files them by card type: Asceticism in THE SETUP (an enchantment), Mithril Coat in THE GEAR (an equipment), Stubborn Denial in THE INSURANCE (an instant), Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood and Steel Hellkite in THE AIR FORCE (Dragons). THE INSURANCE's gloss, 'held up, not cast', describes the job the four instant-speed additions were bought for, yet only Stubborn Denial is in it — the three flash permanents are elsewhere — while the city holds Crux of Fate, a sorcery that can be held up only under Whirlwing. Four of the six are castable at instant speed as printed (Stubborn Denial, plus flash on Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing), and Steel Hellkite, a Dragon, becomes so while Whirlwing is on the battlefield; only Asceticism is a plain sorcery-speed permanent. That sentence is in no card's text.

open_questions.question: On your own turn, with Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge and Sneak Attack on the battlefield, put a nontoken creature in with Sneak Attack. At the beginning of your end step both Sneak Attack's delayed sacrifice and Gadrak's Treasure trigger fire: can you order them (CR 603.3b) so the sacrifice resolves first and Gadrak counts that creature, and does the Treasure arrive before the end step's priority so it can pay for an instant?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Gadrak with Sneak Attack is the only repeatable fodder-to-fuel conversion that spends nothing but {R}: Sneak Attack has no once-per-turn limit and each creature it puts in dies at an end step. The others are one-shots or cost an output: Desolation of Smaug, Crux of Fate's non-Dragon mode and Generous Gift with Gadrak out are single spells; Atsushi, the Blazing Sky pays for its own death (via Sneak Attack, Crux's Dragon mode, Generous Gift or a damage trigger, with no Gadrak needed) but once, since nothing in the 99 returns it; and pointing a repeating damage trigger such as Terror of the Peaks at your own creature spends the damage it exists to deal. absent_stages[0] keeps the no-fodder verdict on the grounds that the payoff side is Gadrak plus one self-cashing Atsushi and that every route eats the deck's own cards; it does not rest on any of them being a one-shot. findings.claim: 'A scan for dies|died returns exactly two cards that turn a death into a resource: Gadrak ... the only card that pays for ANOTHER creature's death; and Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, which pays for its OWN death only (three Treasures, or two impulse-drawn cards)'
findings.note: ROUND-3 FINDING RESOLVED. A sweep of cards.json (97 entries) for \bdies\b|\bdied\b returns exactly Atsushi, the Blazing Sky and Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge. Atsushi reads 'When Atsushi dies, choose one: exile the top two cards ... you may play those cards / Create three Treasure tokens', so it pays for its own death only. Gadrak reads 'At the beginning of your end step, create a Treasure token for each nontoken creature that died this turn', so it pays for any nontoken creature's death and needs Gadrak on the battlefield at the end step ('only while Gadrak itself survives' is right). Generous Gift's Elephant is the spell's own effect and not a death payoff, so leaving it out of this list is correct. The 'sacrific' count of eleven is re-confirmed, with the same eleven names. Mechanically checkable: any 'exactly N cards turn a death into a resource' claim can be swept against oracle dies|died in cards.json.

findings.claim: 'nothing in the 99 returns it from the graveyard or to hand'
findings.note: A cards.json sweep for graveyard|return|owner's hand|into your hand matches seven cards. Breaching Dragonstorm and Roiling Dragonstorm return THEMSELVES. Hellkite Courser returns the commander to the command zone. Herald's Horn, Sarkhan's Triumph and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon put cards from the LIBRARY into hand. Transcendent Dragon exiles a countered spell. None returns a creature from the graveyard or bounces one to hand, so Atsushi converts itself once per game. The Ur-Dragon's attack trigger puts a permanent from hand onto the battlefield, which is not recursion either.

findings.claim: the choosable-kill list: Sneak Attack; Desolation of Smaug; Crux of Fate's two modes; Generous Gift on your own creature; the any-target damage triggers (Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest, Scourge of Valkas, Drakuseth, Smaug)
findings.note: Complete by enumeration. Every 'any target' damage source among the deck's creatures and enchantments is named. The cards left out are rightly left out. Glorybringer hits only a 'non-Dragon creature an opponent controls'. Boros Charm hits only a player or planeswalker. Firespitter Whelp and Thunderbreak Regent hit opponents and players. Steel Hellkite destroys only permanents whose controller it dealt combat damage to, and that can never be you. Swords to Plowshares exiles, so the creature never dies and neither Atsushi nor Gadrak sees it. Generous Gift says 'target permanent', so aiming it at your own creature is legal. Crux's Dragon mode kills Gadrak and Atsushi together, so Gadrak is gone before its end-step trigger and only Atsushi pays: correct. Small wording point: Atsushi is a 4/4, and Drakuseth is the only trigger that deals a FIXED 4. Terror's damage is the entering creature's power, Tempest's and Scourge's is X Dragons, and Smaug's is the Treasure count, so 'a 4-damage trigger' means 'a trigger dealing 4 or more'. Not fail-worthy.

findings.claim: 'Desolation of Smaug (3 to each non-Dragon) and Crux of Fate's non-Dragon mode, which kill the five dorks, Dragonlord's Servant and Dragonspeaker Shaman and leave Gadrak and Atsushi, both Dragons, alive'
findings.note: NON-BLOCKING, and it was in the text before this round: my round-3 note wrongly called this sentence correct. Both Gadrak and Atsushi are Dragons (type lines 'Legendary Creature — Dragon' and 'Legendary Creature — Dragon Spirit'), and both survive both spells: correct. The victim list is imprecise in two places. (a) Crux's non-Dragon mode also destroys Solphim, Mayhem Dominus ('Legendary Creature — Phyrexian Horror', 5/4). The model itself calls Solphim a non-Dragon in map_disagreements and proposed_goldfish_edits. Desolation's 3 damage does NOT kill Solphim, because its toughness is 4. So the two spells do not kill the same set. (b) Faeburrow Elder is a 0/0 that 'gets +1/+1 for each color among permanents you control', and it is itself W/G, so it is at least 2/2. With four or more colours among your permanents (for example The Ur-Dragon on the battlefield, which is WUBRG) it has toughness 4 or more and survives Desolation. 'Kill the five dorks' is true only on boards with three or fewer colours. Neither error moves the verdict's grounds. Both actually strengthen ground two, since Crux also eats a payoff (Solphim). Fix next time the field is touched: 'Crux's non-Dragon mode kills every non-Dragon (the five dorks, Servant, Shaman, Solphim); Desolation kills the same minus Solphim (toughness 4), and minus Faeburrow Elder when you control four or more colours.' Partly mechanical: a 'damage N to each non-Dragon kills X' claim can be checked against type_line and printed toughness in cards.json. Toughness that depends on the board (Faeburrow's 0/0) needs a flag rather than a verdict.
